A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DEnhancer study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original enhancement experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations, Gaussian refinement results, and a 20-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds real-object examples and experiments with further fine-tuned Upscale-A-Video in Appendix D.3–D.4.

M1.justification: The pose-aware encoder, multi-view row attention, epipolar aggregation, augmentation pipeline, and 3D refinement procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same architecture and component specifications.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds qualitative evaluation on realistic object scans from OmniObject3D and complex, richly textured Polycam objects. This provides a limited extension of the retained Objaverse and in-the-wild coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an Upscale-A-Video variant further fine-tuned with the authors' augmentations, comparing it on synthetic multi-view enhancement and Gaussian refinement in Table 8. Existing comparators remain; Unique3D's upscaler was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 introduces an additional baseline training condition using the proposed augmentations. The new real-object evaluation uses BiRefNet background removal as needed. Existing metrics, resolutions, and the main model's training budget are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted severe-corruption examples in Figure 10, real-object generalization examples in Figure 15, and an augmentation-controlled baseline analysis in Table 8 and Figure 16. Existing component ablations and color-correction analyses remain.

E5.justification: The Inception Score results retain identical ± reporting, and the user study retains 20 participants. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including v1 Table 8, now v2 Table 9. New Table 8 reports further-fine-tuned Upscale-A-Video PSNRs of 26.14 and 26.69, versus 25.57 and 26.20 for its earlier configuration; 3DEnhancer retains its lead. New qualitative examples are added, while Figure 5 loses one reconstruction example.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the horizontal-row approximation, epipolar correspondence formulation, fusion weights, and optimization objective are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning generic 3D enhancement, view consistency, controllable texture refinement, and advantages in multi-view enhancement and per-instance optimization.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 expands the explanation of video-baseline limitations through absent camera-pose conditioning and short sequence processing, specifying eight frames for Upscale-A-Video. It interprets the remaining advantage after additional baseline fine-tuning as support for the proposed cross-view mechanisms.

D1.justification: v2 documents BiRefNet preprocessing for the new real-object examples and identifies the augmentations used for extra baseline fine-tuning. It omits v1's explicit statement that evaluation uses four orthogonal views, reducing protocol documentation without establishing an actual change in test-view sampling.

R1.justification: Four references are added: ViewDiff, Deceptive-NeRF/3DGS, OmniObject3D, and BiRefNet. Section 2 adds a brief contrast with Deceptive-NeRF/3DGS's reliance on accurately captured sparse views; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Limited copyediting corrects 'raw attention' to 'row attention,' adjusts terminology, and shortens passages and captions. v2 adds acknowledgements, corresponding-author annotations, and two appendix subsections while retaining the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 10, 15, and 16 and Table 8, renumbering later appendix displays. Tighter spacing and relocated displays compact the main text, and Figure 5 decreases from three object examples to two. The overall layout and most existing visuals are preserved.

improvement.justification: Further fine-tuning Upscale-A-Video with the proposed augmentations provides a stronger comparison while preserving 3DEnhancer's lead. Real-object and severe-corruption examples add limited robustness evidence. These benefits outweigh the small loss of test-view documentation, although generalization evidence remains qualitative and the additional fine-tuning budget is unspecified.
